name.rationale: The name field is required to uniquely identify the AppGateway resource within a project and location.

region.rationale: The region field is used to specify the geographical location of the AppGateway, which can have implications for data residency and latency.

type.description: The type of network connectivity used by the AppGateway. Default value is `TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`. Possible values are: `TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`, `TCP_PROXY`.
type.rationale: The type field is used to specify the network connectivity type for the AppGateway.

host_type.description: The type of hosting used by the AppGateway. Default value is `HOST_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`. Possible values are: `HOST_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`, `GCP_REGIONAL_MIG`.
host_type.rationale: The host type field is used to specify the hosting type for the AppGateway.

logging_config.rationale: Logging provides visibility into gateway activity and supports auditing, monitoring, and incident response.

enable.description: Specifies whether logging is enabled for the AppGateway.
enable.rationale: This must be enabled to ensure security events and traffic handling by the gateway can be traced and reviewed.

display_name.description: An arbitrary user-provided name for the AppGateway.
display_name.rationale: Display name is for user convenience and does not impact security.

labels.description: Resource labels to represent user provided metadata. **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration. Please refer to the field `effective_labels` for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are used for metadata and do not directly impact security.

project.description: If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project field is used to identify the project resource. Some organisations may have policies that restrict which projects can be used, but this is not inherently a security issue.
